என்னதான் கற்றால் என் ... உன்னை அறியாதார் உய்வரோ makes the same point as கற்றதனால் ஆய பயனென்கொல் வாலறிவன் நற்றாள் தொழாஅர் எனின்: learning weighed against the Lord and found useless. The note correctly adds that Pattinathar sets possessions (எப்பொருளும் பெற்றால் என்) beside learning.

பத்தி அடியவர் பச்சிலை இடினும் முத்தி கொடுத்து in the Marudur kovai and போதும் பெறாவிடில் பச்சிலை உண்டு ... நெஞ்சு உண்டு ... இணையாகச் செப்பும் in the Kazhumalam kovai make the same claim, that grace is not priced by the offering, in two works by the same poet. The note describes both fairly.

Pattinathar's எண்டிசை திண்டோள், இருங்கடல் உடை, விண்ணவர் ... விசும்பே நின் ஆகம் matches Tirumular's திசையொடு தேவரும், கடல் மலை ஆதியும் ஆய் நிற்கும், and both add agency: அமைத்தலும் அழித்தலும் ... நின் இயல்பே beside உலகில் தலைவனும் ஆமே. The note's reading of both lines is accurate.

Both define the final place (பேதமற நின்றவிடம்; நின்றிடம்) by a list of negations, Pattinathar's போய் ... போய் ... போய் answering Sivavakkiyar's அற்று ... அற்று, and both negate the religious goods themselves (மா மௌன ராச்சியம்; முத்தி, சத்தி, சம்பு). The note is right that what remains is only a name (பேதமற; சிவாயம்).
links.text_issue: siddhar:1009 விலைந்ததே read as விளைந்ததே.

links.reason: The link needs மாகக் குருவி பறவாமல் கோதாட்டி to mean the mother guarding the infant's life as a bird that might leave the body, but in a venba about the mother's hand that raised him the sky-bird is as easily a lullaby or pet image, and the marker concedes this. The Tamil does not fix the bird as உயிர், so the shared image with புள் பறந்தற்றே is not established.

பொறியாய் புலனாகி பூதபேதப் பிரிவாய் அறிவாகி நின்ற names tattva groups as what the Lord became, which is Tirumular's உடல் உயிர் தத்துவமாய் நிற்கும். The note is accurate that both place the Lord as the tattvas rather than beyond them and that Pattinathar adds அறிவு.

Both refuse deferral in the same terms, இன்று செய்வோம் ... நாளை என்று against இன்றுகொல் அன்றுகொல் என்றுகொல் என்னாது, and the note correctly gives the differing sanction: விடும் (the god lets the postponer go) against பின்றையே நின்றது கூற்றம். The same claim appears in two books with different reasons.

நாதாந்த மூல நடு இருப்பது and நாத முடிவிலே ... இருப்பது both place the goal at the end of sound, with the same verb இருப்பது. The note's addition that Pattiragiriyar passes the texts (வேதாந்த வேதம் எல்லாம் கடந்து) to reach it is in the Tamil.

கன்னி இளங்கமுகு காய்த்தது and கன்னியும் கன்னி அழிந்தனள் ... பெற்றனள் both turn on a virgin that bears, so the echo is real. But கன்னிக் கமுகு can be read simply as a young palm fruiting early, and the Tirumular line that names the bearing is corrupt, so the paradox is firm on neither side.
links.text_issue: tirumanthiram:1118 line 2 (துன்னியங fகைவரைப்) is corrupt.

links.reason: The agreement that even the body is to be left depends on reading பஞ்சவர்கள் ஆண்டிருந்த தேசம் as the body ruled by the five senses; the plainer reading is the Pandavas leaving their kingdom, and the note blends the two. The புழுக்கூடு of line 1 makes the body reading defensible, but the Tamil does not fix it, so the match with உடம்பும் மிகை is a generous one.

Both define the good by abstentions and both name anger (வெங்கோபம்; வெகுளி), but the lists otherwise differ, and the note's claim that both place anger in the heart 'நெஞ்சில் / உள்ளத்து' is false for the Kural: 35 reads அழுக்காறு அவா வெகுளி இன்னாச்சொல் நான்கும் இழுக்கா இயன்றது அறம், with no உள்ளத்து. The structural parallel is real but thin.

The Naladiyar makes the eater's belly a cremation ground (புல்லறிவாளர் வயிறு ... காடே), but Pattinathar's சடக்கடத்துக்கு இரை தேடி makes the body a pot to be fed, not a place of the dead; the 'body as place of the dead' is supplied by the note. Both condemn flesh-eating, which is a shared topic, not a shared image.
links.text_issue: siddhar:269 படங்கடித்து and இடக்கடிக்கும் are hard to construe.

links.reason: பத்துத் திசைக்கும் அடங்காப் பருவம் / எத்திசைக்கும் எங்கும் ... ஏகம் and பத்துத் திசையும் பரம் ஒரு தெய்வம் உண்டு / எத்திக்கு இலர் இல்லை share both the ten directions and the எத்திசை/எத்திக்கு turn. The note is right that Pattinathar's half-stanza has only the pervasion and none of Tirumular's refuge or sea of deeds.

இறைவற்கு ஒரு பச்சிலை யாவர்க்குமாம் and பச்சிலை உண்டு புனல் உண்டு ... நெஞ்சு உண்டு make the same claim with the same word, that the smallest offering suffices. The note's point that Pattinathar goes further to the heart alone (ஏதும் பெறாவிடில் நெஞ்சு உண்டு) is in the Tamil.

Pattinathar's verse is a conventional shrine-list ending கச்சி ஏகம்பம் நண்ணுமினே; it neither limits nor conditions Tirumular's உள்ளம் பெருங்கோயில். The note's 'thinking heart is the condition in both' is not in Tirumular, whose condition is தெள்ளத் தெளிந்தார்க்கு, and the shared word நெஞ்சு/உள்ளம் is all that joins them.

ஓசை மணித் தீபத்தில் ஒன்றி நிற்பது and எறிமணி தான் அகக் காற்றின் விளக்கது both fuse the bell's sound with a lamp into one inner object, a distinctive figure for nada and light together. The note describes both accurately.
links.text_issue: tirumanthiram:2521 அற்றலும் is obscure; the bell-lamp line is clear.

links.reason: The five முன்னே ending in குற்றாலத்தானையே கூறு and அன்றறிவாம் என்னாது அறஞ்செய்க make the same claim, that the only time is before death, and the note correctly separates what is to be done (the name; virtue). Different books, same argument from the end.

பசித்தோர் முகம் பார் set beside உயர் செல்வம் எல்லாம் அன்று என்று இரு, and அற்றார் அழிபசி தீர்த்தல் as the place to store wealth, both make attending to the hungry the right use of what one has. The note's contrast, the Kural redirecting wealth and Pattinathar having dismissed it, is accurate to both texts.

ஆகம் உருக அன்பு உருக என்பு உருக answers அன்போடு உருகி அகங்குழைவார்க்கன்றி, with உருகு and என்பு in both: bones melted by love where Tirumular's bones as firewood (என்பே விறகா) avail nothing. The note slightly overstates in saying both set melting against burning, since only Tirumular names the burning, but the shared claim holds.

உவட்டாத ஆனந்தக் கள் and தேனின் ருசி போல் தெவிட்டாய் share only the non-cloying verb for bliss, a frequent devotional formula; the drinks differ and nothing else in the two verses corresponds. The note is accurate but the shared element is thin.

அருளை விழுங்கும் இருள் and சிவத்தை விழுங்கி ... மும்மலம் use the same verb விழுங்கு for impurity eating the divine, in two nearby stanzas of the same lament. The note is accurate and the shared figure is distinctive within the work.

249's ஊரும் உற்றார் பேரும் பெண்டீர் பிள்ளைகளும் சீரும் செல்வம் ... சதமல்ல returns in 277 as ஊர் நல்லோர் பேர் தாய் பெண் சீர் சிறப்பு ஏர் ... இருந்தென்ன, so the second stanza asks the use of what the first calls impermanent. The note's 'same catalogue' is slightly loose (277 has தாய் and ஏர், not children or wealth) but the development is real.

நான் ... தான் என்று நீ இருந்ததனை அறிவது and தானென்ற பூவை அவனடி சாத்தினால் நானென்று அவனென்கை நல்லதொன்று அன்றே both dissolve the first person into the Lord by pronoun play on நான்/தான். The note's distinction, offering in Tirumular and recognition in Pattiragiriyar, is in the verbs (சாத்தினால்; அறிவது).
links.text_issue: tirumanthiram:1607 last line admits two readings, as the marker notes.

links.reason: Both reason from the suddenness of death to an act now, and both end at the wailing kin: உற்றார் அழுமுன்னே ... ஊரார் சுடுமுன்னே beside தன் கேள் அலறச் சென்றான். The note is accurate and the shared detail makes this more than a stock impermanence pairing.

Both stanzas close with எல்லாப் பிழையும் பொறுத்தருள்வாய் கச்சியேகம்பனே; 245 lists faults of omission (கல்லாப் பிழை ... தொழாப் பிழை), 264 faults of commission by speech, thought, deed, glance and hearing. The note describes both accurately and the complement is the development.

The shared word is மணி, but in 48 it is the bell (ஓசைமணி) and in 820 the gem of மணிவிளக்கு; the lamp is the only common image. 48 never places its lamp in the body, so 'the lamp lit inside the body is the goal in both' rests on the traditional nada-jyoti gloss, not on 48's Tamil.

A walled dwelling full of counted inmates who perish or flee when it ends is a real shared figure (மதிளுடைக் கோயில் / உட்கோட்டை). But 521 says nothing of burning (only மடிந்தார்கள், பட்டார்கள்), and its அறுபது is matched to the ninety-six only by tradition, so the note overstates the match.

Both strip the body to its filth, and Naladiyar's கருந்தோல் that dazzles the fool is exactly the skin Pattinathar lifts. But by the note's own account they aim at different things, desire and the self, so they do not make the same claim; Pattinathar extends the Naladiyar's dissection to the question of 'I'.

Both name the five senses and the four inner instruments in the final state, but 2153 has them understood together (ஒருங்கே உணர்ந்தபின்), while 798 has them made one and steadied (ஒன்றாய்ச் சீலமுற்று). The 'four inner instruments' in 2153 is only a reading of உண்டன நான்கும், and the subject there is unclear, so the agreement is thin.

Both deny that the reality is reached by book or speech (வாசித்தும்/நூல்வழி, பேசாமல்/வாதிகள் பாஷிக்கத் தகாது), a real but stock ineffability topos. The note's 'same three denials' is inaccurate: Arunagirinathar's third is imagined meditation (பாவனை), not worship, and his list is much longer.

Both pair sun and moon becoming one with the breath, but 734 only uses this as a simile for something he confesses he does not know (உயிர்ப்பறியேன்), while 2433 gives the practice. Reading 734's கதிர்மதி as the two breaths depends on the cipher, and 'agrees' overstates a confession set beside an instruction.

960 ends with சொன்னிலை சுருங்கினல்லது நின்னியலறிவோர் யார், and 2955 mocks those who speak the unspeakable (உரையற்றது ஒன்றை உரைசெய்யும் ஊமர்காள்) and gives the vision to still thought. Both make the failure of speech the gate to knowing, and the paradox litany against the 'mutes' is a useful pairing.

Both are poets' confessions of poor verse, but they make different claims. 953 says poor-worded hymns become Veda when they praise Ekambar; Thiruppugazh 313 confesses he lacks devotional poetry and the rapt vow (பரவசம் பற்றிப் பற்றற நிற்கும் பரவ்ரதம்) and asks how his sorrow will end. It nowhere says the name praised redeems the poem, so 'both set the name above the learning' overreads 313.

ஏணி to release is shared and distinctive: 152 sets a ladder (ஏணிவைப்பது) to the unreachable old city (எட்டாப் பழம்பதி), and 126 makes the thirty-six the rungs of the ladder to mukti (படிமுத்தி ஏணி). The note says accurately that only Tirumular names the rungs.

The body as a vessel of flowing filth (மலசலங்கள் பாயும் புழுக்கூடு / ஒன்பது வாய் ... கும்பம்) is a stock image across the corpus, and the two figures (a worm-nest, a nine-holed pot) differ. The note's contrast between another's body and one's own is fair but thin.

Both place the Lord among ghouls and corpses at the cremation ground (பேயுங்கணமும் ... பிணக்காடு / பேய்கள்கூடிப் பிணங்கள்தின்னும் ... காட்டிலே), a real but stock Saiva image. 1461 does not 'approach' the Lord: it asks what kind of life Namban's is and then turns to desire, so the note's common purpose is overstated.
links.text_issue: 1461 is flagged uncertain; how its two halves join is unclear

links.reason: The qualification is real: the trappings of kingship do not shine without Kambar's நீறு. But the note's 'the same horses, elephants, infantry, chariots' misdescribes Kural 381, whose six limbs (படை குடி கூழ் அமைச்சு நட்பு அரண்) are not the fourfold army and parasol. Only படை overlaps.

87's நான்மாண்டு ... முத்திநிலை வந்தடைவ and 346's யான் எனது என்னும் செருக்கு அறுப்பான் ... உயர்ந்த உலகம் புகும் make the same claim: the death of 'I' comes before the higher state. It is the Kural's doctrine voiced in a Siddhar's chain of deaths.

The link rests on one shared word, பூரணம். 2426 is a general challenge to anyone who calls பூரணம் God ('புகல வேண்டும்'), defining it as the sixteen kalas; it does not limit 844's claim about the Lord. The contrast between epithet and technical term is informative but it is a shared-word link, not a qualification.
கண்டுபின்னும் ... நினைப்பதல்லால் (286) and உண்மைகண்டும் உணர்கிலீர் (1046) make the same specific reproach: people see death plainly and it changes nothing. The note attributes both poets correctly.

507's கொண்டான் குருவடிவம் and 1527's இன்னருட் சத்தி குருவென வந்து state the same doctrine, that liberating grace comes in the guru's form. The note flags that the two deeds come from 527, not from 507 itself.

Both describe rousing the base power through the middle channel (சுழுமுனையின் தாள்திறந்து / நடுநாடி ... மூலம் ... எழுப்பி), but that is standard kundalini doctrine and the pairing adds little. 857 does not name the kundalini, and the 'shut door' is 95's own image.

Both have kings with all their pomp end in death (முடிசார்ந்த மன்னரும் ... பிடிசாம்பராய் / யானைத் தலைமிசைக் கொண்ட குடையர் ... துஞ்சினார்). The note rightly separates the Naladiyar's plain impermanence from Pattinathar's கண்டுபின்னும், the point that seeing it does not teach.

Both use a deliberately foul anatomy of women to break desire, a stock method (the marker cites the Naladiyar for both). 359 ends on the poet's own mind (மனம் பற்றியதே), but 574 ends by asking Murugan to save him from the mire (அளறிலழுந்தாமல் ஆட்கொண்டருள்வாயே), so 'both close by turning on the poet's own mind' is overstated.
links.text_issue: 574 has corrupt and obscure words in its foul catalogue

links.reason: Within the same Arutpulambal, 499 asks whether வெட்டவெளி will come (கிட்டாதோ) and 529 says வெட்டவெளி யானேன். The movement from longing to arrival in the same term is a real development.

Both give the woman's toilet item by item, with turmeric (மஞ்சள் / அரிசன), the forehead dot (பொட்டு) and the earring (ஓலை / காதுக் கோலை), and both end with a plea to remove his desire (இட்டத்தை நீ தவிர்ப்பாய் / ஆசை ... துயரற பாதம் தருவாய்). The shared catalogue is distinctive.
629's பாலர் பெண்டீர் மெய்யென்று and 1044's மக்கள் பெண்டீர் சுற்றம் ... மாயை say the same thing from two sides: the fault is taking kin as real. The note attributes the poets correctly.

Both quote the conventional similes for a woman's limbs in order to refuse them: cloud for hair (முகில் / கார்), lily for eyes (கழுநீர் / சேல்), Meru or lotus bud for breasts. Pattinathar answers each with its matter, and Arunagirinathar asks not to drown in the eyes' maya. It is a distinctive shared device.

Both pair the tortoise's drawing in of the five (ஆமை ... ஐந்தடக்கம் / ஆமை அகத்தினில் அஞ்சம் அடங்கிடும்) with ஊமை, and both carry restraint into silence or namelessness. ஊமை means a mute in 20 and the unspoken letter in 2158, but the co-occurrence of ஆமை and ஊமை is striking and the note does not overclaim.

Both bring the body that was prized (நல்லுடல், the body dressed in silk and sandal) to its stink (நாறும்) and the burning ground (சுடலை), the stock end of the body. The specific points differ, 969's jealousy and 811's funeral show, so the agreement is generic.
links.text_issue: 811 has lacunae marked [***]

links.reason: 127's சாதிவகை இல்லாமல் and 972's பிறப்பொக்கும் எல்லா உயிர்க்கும் both deny distinction by birth. The note fairly says the Kural keeps a distinction by செய்தொழில் that the pulambal does not.

The body as a skin bag (சோற்றுத் துருத்தி / தோற்பை) is a common image in both corpora, and the uses differ: 46 is weariness of carrying it, and 1250 is the maya of taking it as 'I' (யானாக நோக்கும்). The pairing is real but generic.

311 says forest, wind-eating, rags and bowl are nothing without உள்ளன்பு, and 321 longs for exactly that outward life (இல்லந் துறந்து ... இரந்து). 311 supplies the condition under which 321's wish counts, and the note states it carefully.

Both start the body from seed and womb (ஒழுகிய விந்து ... சுரோணிதம் / விழுந்தது லிங்கம் விரிந்தது யோனி), but 455's faculties rise and hide at the brow and crown (நுதல் உச்சி உள்ளே ஒளித்ததே), while 808 tells the child's growth. The common ground is the topic of embryology rather than a shared claim.
links.text_issue: 455 flagged uncertain; 808 has lacunae

links.reason: Only காமக் குரோதம் (445) and ஆசை ... ரோசம் (2388) are shared. 445's second line is நாமே அரசென்று நாடோறு மெண்ணுதே, the ego's claim to rule, and it says nothing about kin, so the note's 'his kin-desire refuses to forget' invents half of the match.

Farming carried into the mind is real, with manure (மெய்யெனும் எருவை), weeding (களையறக் களைந்து) and a fence (சாந்த வேலி) against the five cattle. But the note misstates the order: in 821 the fence is built before the sprout and the weeding (வேலி கோலி வாய்ந்தபின் ... முளைத்து ... களைந்து), not after it. The Kural's point is a ranking of care, not a sequence Pattinathar follows.

311 says true lovers reach release even at home with women (நாரியர்பால் வீடே யிருப்பினும்), and 347 says those free of attachment look like worldly people (உலகத்தவர்போலிருப்பர்). Together they make outward conduct no test of renunciation, which is a real development.
links.text_issue: 347 flagged uncertain at மாத்தானவத்தை

links.reason: The lotus leaf on water untouched by it (தாமரை இலைபோல் / நீரினோடு கூடிநின்றும் நீரிலாத) is the stock image of detachment. The note's contrast, the Lord's way of being in the world against the devotee's, rests on one of two readings of பண்டிதப் பராபரம், which may instead be the sage.

2614 explicitly denies the Lord is in the temple (கோயிலுள் ளானலன்) and places him in the heart. 835 places the light in the one-pointed mind but still praises Marudur and does not deny the shrine, so 'not the building' overstates 835. The inner-not-outer pairing is close to the stock attack.

Both are a poet's conventional apology, but they make different claims. 965 asks the learned to forgive a madman's recital (பேயனாகி ஓதிடும் பிழைபொறுக்க), while 233 confesses he does not know himself (என்னையே நான் அறியேன்) and asks the ancients to accept his words. The pairing is the shared modesty topos.

Both tell the possessor to share wealth because it is not his to keep: the Naladiyar because it turns like a cart wheel (சகடக்கால் போல), and Pattinathar because it came from former deeds (முற்றொடர்பிற் செய்த முறைமையால்) and was owed to அற்றவர் and கற்றவர். The note's 'adds' fairly marks what Pattinathar contributes.

Body as excess for those cutting off birth (உடம்பும் மிகை) and the body as one's own enemy (தன்னுடம்பு தானே தனக்குப் பகை) are the same view. The note rightly frames Pattinathar's verse as the regret of one who did not hold it.

Both confess that their words cannot reach the god: 962's இன்னாப் புன்மொழி நின்னிடையணுகா, and 313's lack of devotional poetry and learning spent on argument. 962 lays அறிவு itself at the feet along with everything else. The shared confession of words and learning that fail is specific.

Bangles slipping from the wrist (வெள்வளை போயின / இறைஇறவா நின்ற வளை) as the sign of a woman wasted by a man's leaving is the akam image, carried here into Pattinathar's devotional street scene. The shared use is precise and meaningful.

71 names only the hexagon of air (வாயு அறுகோணம்) and Mahesvara. The square, the circle, Sadasiva and the 'same order' all come from 72, which is not in the packet, while 1745's hexagon belongs to Shakti. Within these two verses the link is one shared word.

முப்பாழ் is shared technical vocabulary and 115 does void the three voids and then the first (முதற்பாழும் சூனியமாய் அப்பாழும் பாழாய்), ending in அன்பு. But 115 never takes up Tirumular's mapping of the voids to soul, Supreme and union, so 'pushes the series one step further' is the proposer's construction on a verse flagged uncertain.

151 places the goal past அட்டாங்கயோகம் twice over (அப்பாலுக்கு அப்பால்); 187 names what that leaving looks like: நிட்டைதனை விட்டு, letting நினைவறிவு slip, mingling in வெட்டவெளி. The step from 'beyond the practice' to 'leaving the practice's fixity' is a real development.

Both stanzas carry the refrain of the hunter's leavings (சிலைதொட்ட / சிலையார்கை வேடன் எச்சில் தின்றான்), and 673 adds the sale to the bard (விலையாகிப் பாணனுக்கு ... அடிமைப்பட்டது) and names the heart's fault as ஆணவம். The note describes both accurately and the contrast of the stooping Lord with the proud heart is in 673's Tamil.

Both read the cosmos as the god's adornment: தன்னொளி ஆரம் தாராகணமே against வானுடு மாலை (stars as garland), with the sea as உடை in 954 and மஞ்சன சாலை in 1725, the directions as shoulders (எண்டிசை திண்டோள்) against Nandi's garment. The note states the shared and differing members correctly.

240's சூத்திரப்பாவை on its நன்னார் is clear; Tirumanthiram 2344's பொய்க்கரி ஆட்டும் is an obscure phrase (toy elephant or false image) in a verse flagged uncertain, and its point is the five acts, not the soul's dependence. The Lord-as-puppeteer image is common enough that the pairing teaches little beyond the shared figure.

1010 argues சாதிபேதம் has no substance; 360's எந்தச் சாதியிலும் இரக்கத் துணிந்து is the renunciant's indifference to the giver, not an application of Sivavakkiyar's argument, and the poets are different. The connection is a shared anti-caste stance, which the brief counts as thin; 'develops' overstates it.

Same work, same frame (போட்டு உனை அடைவது எக்காலம்) and the same துருத்தி: 46's சோற்றுத் துருத்தி, a skin of rice, and 128's காற்று ஊதும் துருத்தி, the breathing body. The note's 'filled with food in one and with breath in the other' is exactly what the Tamil gives.

62 has only the melting (ஆகம் ... அன்பு ... என்பு உருக) and போக அனுபூதி; the tears and honey the note relies on come from 61 and 66, not the linked verse, so 'the sequence melting, tears, nectar is the same in both' is not true of the pair. Tirumanthiram 2778's melting is also caused by seeing the dance, which 62 does not mention.

1666 makes the ash armour (கவசத் திருநீறு) that ends deeds and brings சிவகதி; 883 says kingship and drum will not shine (பொலியாது) without Kambar's ash on the brow, which is the ash as glory or mark, not protection. 'Both make the ash the real protection' misstates 883; what remains is a shared topic.
links.text_issue: Tirumanthiram 1666 line 1 has a corrupt 'பூசுng' (Latin letters in the Tamil).

links.reason: The distinctive formula நீயும் நானுமாய் appears in both: 304 asks for a day when நீயும் நானுமாய் stand in the வெளி beyond the tattvas, and 858 asks for the bliss of ஏக போகமாய் நீயு நானுமாய் after இருவினை, மும்மலம், இறவி and பிறவி end. 'Beyond the body and its tattvas' fits 304 better than 858, but the shared aim is real.

நீர்க்குமிழி யாம் உடல் against படுமழை மொக்குளின் ... யாக்கை: the same bubble for the body, and the contrast is real, since the Naladiyar's திண்ணறிவாளர் see it and end their தடுமாற்றம் while Pattinathar's thought takes it as நித்தியம். The image is stock, but the pairing of the wise with the deluded mind is apt.

The wasp-and-worm figure is in both (குளவி உருக்கொண்டது; நினைத்தவண்ணம் ஆயிடும் ... பறந்ததும்பி). But 169 also states the transformation (புழு குளவி உருக்கொண்டது போல்), so the note's contrast, a lesson in thinking for Sivavakkiyar against a figure of confinement for Pattiragiriyar, overstates the difference; the image is stock.

773's தேனின் ருசி போல் தெவிட்டாய் is about not cloying; 325's ஓவாத தேறல், சுத்த மது in the chapter கள்ளுண்ணாமை is liquor-language for bliss that does not cease. Sweet drink for bliss is generic, and 'both answer the same doubt' is a frame the note supplies; 325's last line is obscure.

The same phrase மாணிக்கத்துள் ஒளி recurs in the same lament: in 550 he dwells mingled (மருவி இருந்தாண்டி) like that light, in 563 he is that light for those who set a noble mind (மாட்சி மனம் வைத்தார்க்கு). The note's indwelling vs condition distinction matches the Tamil.

Dead while living in both: 209's மாண்டிருப்பது with birth, death, speech, breath, memory and forgetting removed, and 1671's செத்துத் திரிவர் சிவஞானியோர் while பொறியும் உடலும் remain. The note's point that மூச்சும் அற்று adds a yogic mark is fair.

156's ஆதிமுதல் ஆகிநின்ற ... அட்சரம் echoes the Kural's அகர முதல ... ஆதி, but the letter it names is அரி, and the note itself says the link holds only on reading அரி as அ, one of two readings in a verse flagged uncertain. A link resting on an unfixed reading is weak.

Both list kinds of birth (கல், மரம், கயல், பறவை, புல் / குருவி, கழுகு, நரி, மிருகம், புழு, குறவை, கரி, மரம்), but the birth-list is stock, and in 263 the marker allows the list may be insults the crowd throws rather than births. The agreement is generic.

காற்றுத் துருத்தி and பொள்ளுற்ற காற்பை are the same stock wind-bag body. The note fairly gives 652's turn to not feeding the hungry (அன்னம் பசித்தோருக்கு ஈயாமல்), but the shared image is a commonplace and 534 is largely obscure.

987's ஓடம் is the body, to be made firm (உறுதிபண்ணி) while it lasts before the வெளி; in 961 the body is the sea (உடல் இருங்கடல்) and the Lord's feet the ship (நாவாயாகிய ... நின்பாதம்). The same voyage figure with the body in opposite roles is a real and instructive contrast.
links.text_issue: Siddhar 961 has misprints: ஐவகைனெடுங்காற், உருகிய்வார்வப், தூம்ச்சோதிச்.

links.reason: Naladiyar 365 ranks தவமுயன்று வாழ்தல் first and இனியார்கண் தங்கல் second; 830 sets the ascetics who torment themselves for முத்தி against 'we' who lived with women and kin yet, keeping the ஐந்தெழுத்து, have not lost முத்தி, and the stone that falls whoever throws it says the means do not matter. The note names the reading the conflict depends on.

Both itemize the body by the physician's humours (மெய்வளி ... பித்து, ஐவகை காற்று; பித்துருத்தன், முக்குற்றம்), but this is the same domain, the body, not a pattern carried into a different one. As a shared image of the medical body it is real but stock.

1010 argues caste from the body's single stuff (பூதம் ஐந்தும் ஒன்றலோ); 709 confesses not knowing that குலம் ஒன்றாய் நீ படைத்த, with மலபாண்டம் only as where he stayed deluded, not an argument from the body. 'Both deny caste any ground in the body's stuff' overstates 709, and குறை is ambiguous; the shared anti-caste stance is stock.

505's வாக்கு மனாதீத state, reached because the guru of grace strikes (தாக்கும் அருட்குருவே), and 1593's உரையற்று உணர்வற்று ... சொரூபத்து இருத்தனன் சொல்லிறந்தோமே both make the passage past words the Lord's act on the poet. The formula is common, but the agent-of-grace point is in both verses.
links.text_issue: Siddhar 505 வசோகசத்தில் looks corrupt (perhaps அசோக சத்து).

links.reason: 771 says the Lord stood (நின்றனையே, second person governing all three) as பாசம் in the body, பசு as life and பொருள; 115 keeps பதி, பசு, பாசம் as three beginningless realities that cannot reach pati. On the Siddhanta reading the identification is incompatible, and the note states that dependency and the monist alternative.

The Kural's sleep and waking makes death and birth continuous; 26 asks to know the வகை of dying and returning, with a lamp-and-darkness image. That fits only if மாண்டு பிழைத்து means rebirth rather than 'nearly dying and surviving', and asking to know the mechanism is not the Kural's calm claim.

1075 lists சாதிபேதம் among the forms the one became; 722 lists the stock seven births (விலங்கு, புள், ஊர்வன, அசரம், விண்ணவர், நீர்ச்சாதி, மனுக்குலங்கள்) and says the poet does not know the intent. Caste is the proposer's import into 722, where சாதி means kind; the shared claim is the generic one-into-many.

38 is the poet's own lament at வெம்பித் திரிகை for கும்பிக்கு இரை; 1480 satirizes costumed yogis (மாடுகள்) who leave the wife (தேவியை அலையவிட்டு) and beg பருக்கை. Begging for the belly is common to both, but the targets and modes differ, and the pairing is a stock attack.

Both stanzas use Tirumular's முப்பாழ் and முதற்பாழ் to place the Lord: in 618 beyond the three as முதற்பாழ், swallowing the poet, and in 639 dancing beyond (அப்பாழுக்கு அப்பால் நின்று ஆடும்) while the heart trusts இப்பாழாம் வாழ்வு. The note slightly blurs 639, where he is beyond the first void rather than as it, but the shared vocabulary is a real, pointed echo.
links.text_issue: Siddhar 639 துப்பாழாய் is obscure and may be corrupt.

links.reason: The magnet is in both (காந்தம் ... இரும்பை / காந்தமொடு ஊசி), and 'one magnet pulls down, the other up' is a good contrast. But 124 asks to be pulled (பாய்ந்து பிடித்திழுத்து உன் பாதத்தில் வைப்பது), not released from a pull, so 'both ask for the same release from the pull' is false of 124.

163 makes the poet the archer (மனதை வில்லாக்கி ... அறிவை அம்பாக்கி எய்வது); the next verse has the Lord shoot him (என்னை இறக்க எய்தே) and wipe out his பழி. The reversal of the archer in the same verb across adjacent verses is a real development.
links.text_issue: Siddhar 164 is compressed; the line division of வெளியில் வைத்தே ஒளித்து is unsure.

links.reason: தூரியினில் மீன் and சமுசார வலை மீன் are both the trapped self, a stock figure. 566 asks for முடியாத பதம், the unending state, so 'in both the way out is the feet' strains பதம்; the pairing adds little.

190 asks to see past pleasures (உண்டதுவும் ... இன்பம் கண்டதுவும்) as the Lord; 211 asks to remove the dream (கனவு) of desire. Sacralizing versus removing desire is a possible tension, but the past tense of 190 makes the licence reading unlikely, as the note concedes; on the likely reading they agree.

555's கல்வியல்ல கேள்வியல்ல கைகாட்டும் காரணம் denies exactly the routes Kural 356 affirms (கற்று ... மெய்ப்பொருள் கண்டார்). The note attributes 'learning texts' to Parimelazhagar where he speaks of hearing from a teacher, but since 555 denies கேள்வி too, the tension stands on either reading.

99 says the பல்கலை that chatter cannot reach (எட்டா) the object; 136 has the arts examined to the end (ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்ததன்பின்) before the truth is seen. 'Not skipped but exhausted' accurately states the development.

Naladiyar 6 says no one here (ஈங்கில்லை) leapt clear of கூற்றம்; 908 cites the Markandeya miracle at Kadavur (கொல்கின்ற கூற்றைக் குமைத்த). A divine exception for one devotee against a rule about ordinary men is different situations, not incompatible claims, as the note half admits.

Kural 380 says nothing is stronger than ஊழ், which arrives first; 310 says rolling under devotees' feet is விதியேட்டைக் கிழிப்பது, tearing the leaf of fate. On the plain reading of both the claims conflict, and the note names that reading.

Naladiyar 11's மன்னா இளமை மகிழ்ந்தாரே கோல்ஊன்றி இன்னாங்கு எழுந்திருப்பார் is drawn out in 809 from வாழ் பதினாறு பிராயம் through நரைதிரை to செங்கையில் ஓர் தடி. Same claim, same staff and grey hair, and the note is right that the Naladiyar states the lesson 809 leaves implicit.
links.text_issue: Siddhar 809 ends mid-sentence (the stanza continues) and has a stray mark in செங்கையினி்லோர்.

links.reason: Both speak of bliss past the working mind (சிந்தனை யற்று ... ஆனந்த நித்திரை; சித்தம் உருக்கி ... சிவானந்தம் விட்டிடா), but sleep and liquor are different images and the 'does not lift' point rests on 325's obscure last line. The agreement is the generic one of unbroken bliss.

Naladiyar 303's worthy man approaches only those who say அகம்புகுமின் உண்ணுமின்; 416 will not go even if called insistently (பெருக்க அழைத்தாலும் போகேன்) and eats only if food is brought to him. Removing the one exception is exactly a qualification, and the note is accurate.

Both end on the cremation log (கட்டையில் வேக / தழல்முருடு ஏறி), but 448's point is the delusion of permanence despite seeing it, not 'the body's care', and 2086's first line is obscure. The shared theme of mortality is stock.

191 only asks when it will know what was heard as ஈம், what stood within and what was said as ஓம்; 2444 assigns seed-syllables (ஆம், ஓம், வாம், பாம்) to body-places. Neither verse says the heard sound and the syllable are 'the same thing in the body'; the link rests on the shared word ஓம்.

TM 151 has மையிட்ட கண்ணாளும் மாடும் இருக்கவே, wife and wealth stay while the man goes; 642 has the fine gold (காணிப்பொன்) not seen coming along when Yama takes the hand. A direct agreement on wealth staying behind at death, across two books.

Both name வாதனை as something passed in a sequence of leavings: 805 drops வாதனை, நிஷ்டை and மாமௌனராச்சியம்; TM 2495 leaves the maya void, the bodha void and the traces of cause and effect. The Tamil (உபசாந்த முப்பாழ் விட தீருமே) actually has even the void of calm left, which the note softens to 'ends in' it, but the claim that the attainments themselves are left holds.

TM 185 கன்றிய காலன் கருக்குழி வைத்தபின் and 25 கருப்படுத்தி என்னை யமன் கைப்பிடித்து share the specific figure of Death as the one who sets a person back into the womb. The note's added contrast with உருப்படுத்தி is accurate to 25.

TM 41's புனஞ்செய்த நெஞ்சு and 821's நெஞ்சப் புனத்து are the same figure of the heart as a cleared field, and 821 works it out stage by stage to the Lord as the ripe fruit (மாணிக்கத் தீங்கனி ... கைவர). A distinctive shared image fairly described.

நீர்மேல் குமிழி / கழிகின்ற நீரிற் குமிழி is the commonest Tamil figure for the body's impermanence. The note's contrast (தாரகம் as false support vs. the body going into the Supreme, போம் அப்பரத்தே) is accurate and mildly instructive, but the shared image is stock.

Both trace the same sequence with the blow at the end: 260 கைதான் வறளின் போய்வாரும் என்று நடுத்தலைக்கே குட்டும்; Thiruppugazh 33 வருபொருள் அளவில் உருக்கி ... வனைமனை புகுதில் அடித்துப் போக்கவும். Stock charge, but the shared specifics (love lasting as long as money, then a beating) make the agreement exact.

சூத்திரம் recurs, but as two different things: the puppeteer's string that makes the poet dance (140) and, in 150, something that flies when பட்டம் அற்று காதற்று. A 'kite-string flying without the kite' is an odd reading; more likely the cut kite flies off. The bound/free contrast the note draws depends on that uncertain reading.
links.text_issue: 150 line 1 (பட்டம் அற்றுக் காதற்றில் பறந்தாடும் சூத்திரம்) is obscure; the string-flies-alone reading is doubtful.

links.reason: The note itself concedes that TM 930 removes the three malas (மும்மலம் கூப்பிட்டுப் போமே) by a chakra-mantra, while 840 removes sins (பாவங்கள் ... கரந்து) by once saying the shrine's name. What remains is the generic idea that a holy word purifies.

389 refuses to praise stone, stucco and copper images and keeps the feet within (உள்ளேயிருத்துவது); TM 725 turns from contempt of the body to cherishing it as உத்தமன் கோயில். Both move worship inward, but this is not a different domain, and the contrast the note draws on the body depends on 387, which is not in the packet.

Both deny that the Veda gives knowledge of the Lord and both place it in கருத்து (608 கருத்துடையோர், 982 கருத்துளே உணர்ந்தபின்), which is a real point of contact. But the denial of Veda-recitation is a stock Siddhar attack, and 'place knowing after reciting' misstates both verses.

329 lists loincloth, porch, leaves, water and the Lord's name as enough and does not mention begging (இரத்தல்); the begging claim comes from 345. The note itself admits the Kural speaks of want forced on a man and Pattinathar of chosen want, which is different situations, not incompatible claims.

Both tell Ravana crushed under the toe and then given a sword (886 நற்கைவாள் ... அளித்தார்; TP 312 தசமுகன் கைக்குக் கட்கம் அளிக்கும்). Accurate, but this is a stock puranic episode told the same way everywhere, so the pairing teaches little.

142 denies that reading, speech and worship (வாசித்தும், பூசித்தும்) show the reality; 977 asks whether the Veda helps when வேர்த்து இரைப்பு comes. A true but stock shared attack on scripture-recitation; nothing specific is learned from the pairing.

TM 1506 says recitation, worship and flowers without love leave the mind like a stone in a mossy pond; 548 says that without bathing the image and plucking flowers the heart became வெறும் பாழ். 548 may be a lament for omitted worship as easily as an advance beyond it, so 'develops' leans on one reading; the link is mostly the shared flowers.

89 asks to have died before the soul in its cage falls (மாண்டுவிழும் முன்னே நான் மாண்டிருப்பது), and 1598 describes the true knower as செத்தாரைப் போலத் திரியும் and asks what use cymbals are to him. The same figure of the living dead, fairly described as a wish in one and a state in the other.
links.text_issue: 1598 is unmarked in the corpus.

links.reason: The tension needs 795 to make the fourth state final, but 795 only says the heart walked in நாலாம்பதம், in a work that goes on (805) to leave further attainments; 973's துரியமும் கடந்து need not contradict a stage. The note fairly flags the sayujya reading, which removes the conflict.

TM 1006 offers இந்திரன் செல்வம் and எண்சித்தி in sequence before release; 818's servants push away இந்திரச் செல்வமும் எட்டுச் சித்தியும் வந்துழி வந்துழி. The same pair of gifts promised in one text and refused in the other; 'qualifies' fits since 818 does not deny that they come.

Both refer to the Markandeya episode: 897 the foot set on the neck of இடிகுரற் கூற்று, 908 the Kadavur Brahmin saved and கொல்கின்ற கூற்றைக் குமைத்த. 908 does not take up the foot or extend 897's idea; it is the same story named twice in one series, so 'develops' overstates it.

1044 says children, wives and kin are maya and cannot come along (வந்துகூடலாகுமோ?) when Death calls, so the kin-bond does leave; 439 says the desire for kin will not let go (மறக்கேனே யென்குதே). The note's 'both treat the bond of kin as the thing that does not leave' contradicts 1044.

Both pair ஓங்காரம் with ஆங்காரம்: TM 1556 has the light in Om rise yet the ego-free experience (ஆங்காரமற்ற அனுபவம்) not gained, while 524 has both ஓங்காரம் and ஆங்காரம் ruined together. The shared rhyme-pair makes the development specific, and the note describes it fairly.

TM 2137 reproaches those who call the body மலம்; 319 calls the woman's sex மலக்குழி in a verse against lust. The note admits this narrows the conflict; it would be much stronger with 849's உடலாம் முழுமலம், and here the clash is partial.

TM 272 says even என்பே விறகா austerity does not reach the gem without melting love; 830 lists the five fires, the water and the plucked hair, and says the luxury-livers who kept the five letters did not lose release (கல்லே போல் ... நின் நாமம் நவின்றோர் வழார்). Both deny that bodily suffering is the cause of attainment. The note is accurate, though one puts love and the other the name in its place.

807 says the heart won நீதிகுருவின் திருத்தாள்; TM 232 makes turiya samadhi the reaching of குருபதம். The guru's feet are shared, but 807 names no turiya or highest state; the identification depends on 795, which is not in this pair.

996 has the Lord enter the heart and make it his temple (கோயில் கொண்டனன்); 607 has him set his feet in a stone heart like a lily blooming. The point that the Lord acts is fair, but 607 has no shrine, and grace indwelling the heart is a generic bhakti claim.

72 alone names only Sadasiva in the circular path (வட்டவழி); the five-god ladder the note matches with TM 1731's ordered list is in 68 to 71, outside the packet. The marker's nuance also calls Sadasiva the sixth in a five-god list, so the claimed match is unverified here.

TM 2483 has the three voids where words cease (சொல்லறும் முப்பாழ்); 622 names those who know முப்பாழ் as the elders who will forgive his faulty similes. 622 says nothing about speech breaking down in the voids; the link is the shared term முப்பாழ் with an inferred connection.

In Kural 332 the gathering and dispersal of the theatre crowd (கூத்தாட்டு அவைக் குழாம்) is the simile for wealth's coming and going. In 292 கைவைத்த நாடகசாலை is just one of the royal possessions asked after ('where is it?'), not a figure for wealth. Same word, different function.
புலித்தோல் is Siva's standard iconography, shared with the bull, ash and crescent in countless verses. The two verses share only that stock mark; nothing in the pairing is specific.

TM 145's townsfolk do mourn (ஒலிக்க அழுதிட்டு) and then forget (நினைப்பொழிந்தார்), so calling it a 'refusal to mourn' misdescribes them. There is a real contrast between worldly forgetting and 399's non-grieving because எல்லாம் சிவமயம், but the note's parallel is overstated.
Muyalakan under the dancing foot is stock Nataraja iconography (TM 2774 அங்கார் முயலகன்; 492 தாக்கு முயலகன் தாண்டவம்). The cosmic vs iconic contrast is fair but thin.

TM 1662 makes ash the first emblem; 467 complains that the Lord did not give the ash he wears (பூசிய நீற்றைப் புனையென் றளித்தையிலை). The rudraksha and the earrings come from 468, not this verse, and a complaint about not being marked is not quite the same claim as a list of emblems.

849 makes the body முழுமலம் and failing to see it the cause of lust; TM 725 tells of once holding the body இழுக்கு and now cherishing it as உத்தமன் கோயில். A real conflict on the value of the body, and the note names the reading it rests on, though 'written against exactly that doctrine' overstates the historical point.

969 has the fine body stink (நாறும் இந்த நல்லுடல்) once Death calls; 630 gives the living body பிணவாசம் already, while money-lust serves it. The note fairly marks the shift from the dead to the living body, which is a development rather than a plain agreement.

Both take எச்சில் as the test case for purity rules: 1113 turns it on the keeper (கண்டஎச்சில் கையலோ ... கொண்டசுத்தம் ஏதடா), and 426 has one examine the எச்சில் itself until ஒருமை shows and the mind is நிராமயம். 426 really does carry the refutation into a contemplative use.
links.text_issue: 1113 line 1 (உண்டகல்லை) is hard and may be corrupt.

links.reason: 357 makes rag, bowl and porch the குறைவற்ற செல்வம்; 429 says the freed mind stays in மோனம் whatever the work or austerity (எந்தொழிலைச் செய்தாலும்), like the water-carrier whose mind is on the pot. The later verse limits the beggar's marks to non-essential, which is a fair qualification within one poet.

The anril of lore that never parts from its mate is shared (N 376 புணர்பிரியா அன்றில்; 218 அன்றிலைப்போல்), and the lover-to-grace shift is real. But the bird is a stock figure, and 218's first line is uncertain, so the note's reading of it is built on shaky text.
links.text_issue: 218 line 1 இணை பிரிந்தபோதல் இன்பமுறும் is likely faulty (the anril should have joy only when not parted).

links.reason: TM 1527 இன்னருட் சத்தி குருவென வந்து and 119 அருளாய் உருவாகி ... குருவாக வந்து state the same doctrine, grace itself arriving as the guru, in nearly the same words. A specific agreement.

TM 1616 makes Siva the model renouncer who eats alms (உண்பது பிச்சை). In 351 பரிவாகப் பிச்சை பகரும் என்றானை may as well mean he kindly told the poet to go and beg (the initiation into mendicancy) as that he begged from him; the note's 'Siva as beggar' rests on one reading of an uncertain verse.

Siva who drank the poison for others (TM 2815 மிக்கார் அமுதுண்ண நஞ்சுண்ட; 30 அண்டருக்காய் நஞ்சருந்தி) is a stock epithet. The shared image is real but generic, and the note's contrast is between parts of the verses that do not touch.

Both deny caste to the one who has reached: 535's rhetorical சாதியிற் கூட்டுவாரோ? சாத்திரத்துக் குள்ளாமோ? after உள்ளபடி ஆச்சு, and 2957's குலமில்லை for those who set Nandi in love by ஞானம். The pairing is about the realised state, not a stock attack, and the note reads both fairly.
A precise shared measure of kin love: 157's ஊர்த்துறைக் காலே ஒழிவர் and 238's மயானங் குறுகியப்பால் எட்டி யடிவைப்ப ரோ? both mark the spot where wife and children stop. The note is accurate to both.

களிம்பு on copper is the shared figure: 183's செம்பில் களிம்புபோல் for the three malas and 114's களிம்பறுத்தான் for Nandi's cutting it away. The note's contrast, cut in Tirumular and still asked for in Pattiragiriyar, holds.

Both verses use the கெண்டை fish (தூண்டிலகப்பட்டுத் துடிகெண்டை in 661, நஞ்சுண்டகெண்டை in 668) in the same refrain chapter, a real shared image. But the note's 'same fish, caught then dying' is imposed: the two are separate similes for separate failures (neglecting the guru, failing to seize the light), so 'develops' overstates.
links.text_issue: 668 line 1 (அஞ்சுமுருவாகியைமூன்றுமெட்டுமொன்றாய்) is unkeyed cipher and may be corrupt.

links.reason: நாலாம் பதம் in 104 may be turiya or sayujya, and the note rightly makes the link conditional. Even on the turiya reading, 104 is only a wish to reach the fourth state, so 2264's warning (உன்னும் துரியமும் ஈசனோடு ஒன்றாக்கால் பின்னையும் வந்து பிறந்திடும்) qualifies a claim 104 does not quite make. The connection is thin.

127 asks to live சாதிவகை இல்லாமல் on Kapila's agama, but 1008 only lists சாதிபேத அற்றது among questions (what is it that is free of caste distinction?) in the seedless seed. That is not a refusal of caste, so the note's 'both refuse caste' rests on stretching one phrase in a list of questions.

Both set the search outside against the one within: காசிவரைபோய்த் திரிந்து காலலுத்தேன் against ஊருநாடு காடுமோடி உழன்றுதேடும் ஊமைகாள். This is the stock Siddhar attack on pilgrimage. The வாசி/பராபரம் difference the note points to is real but small.

நாலாம்பதம் and துரியம் link the two, but 795 leaves the மேலாம் பதங்கள் behind, while 1483's துரியர் have left துன்மார்க்கம், the evil path. Those are different things, so the note's 'both place it after an examination that rejects what came before' does not fit 1483, and the turiya reading of 795 is itself uncertain.

229 does not uphold Vedanta as a text to keep. It redefines வேதாந்தம் as வேட்கை ஒழிந்திடம், the place where craving ends, and mocks Brahmins who hear without effect. So 33's leaving வேதாந்தவேதம் எல்லாம் for நிட்டை does not contradict it. The note itself concedes the agreeing reading, and the 'tension' rests on the shared word.

Refuge at the feet (அடிமலர்க் கமலத்துக் கபயம் / திருவடி நீழல் சரண்) is a common devotional formula. The seas differ in role: 1451's வினைக்கடல் is kept off by refuge, while 302's பவக்கடல் is the voyage of the body-ship being laid down. Real but generic.

Both deny the I/you difference in union and take honey for its bliss: நானேநீநீயேநான் … தேனின்ருசியதுபோற் றெவிட்டாய் and நானென நீயென வேறில்லை … தேனென இன்பம். The coincidence of the claim and the figure is specific, and the note states it exactly.

ஆசைக் கயிற்றி லாடும் பம்பரம் is verbatim in both agavals, and the two bodies-as-vessels lists run parallel (இருவினைப் பெட்டகம் / இருவினை விலங்கு, the மரக்கலம்). One slip: the 'bellows for rice' (சோற்றுத் துருத்தி) is only in 301, since 302's bellows kindles anger. The describe-then-hand-over contrast is accurate.

மாணிக்கத் துள்ளளிபோல் மருவி and கல்லொளி போலக் கலந்துள் ளிருந்திடும் are the same figure of a light inside a gem, and both pair it with the limit of speech (பேசாப் பெருமை / சொல்லிடில் தூராதி தூரம்). A close and meaningful match.
101's ஓடாமல் ஓடி … தேடாமல் answers 967's ஓடிஓடி … நாடிநாடி after the உட்கலந்த சோதி: the same diagnosis that the light is within, with a verbal echo of the running and seeking. The note is accurate.

Both use the poet's self-image as a madman reciting (பித்துப் பிதற்றிலும் / பேயனாகி ஓதிடும்), the conventional அவையடக்கம். But 953 is the hundredth and closing stanza, not a preface as the note says, and the shared modesty topos is thin.
Both ask whether kin will help at death: மாளும்போது உதவுவரோ and மறலிவந்து அழைத்தபோது வந்துகூடலாகுமோ. This is the stock nilaiyamai question, and the pairing adds little beyond it.

Both verses work on I, you and a third (நான் யாரோ நீ யாரோ … தான் யாரோ; நான் … நீ … நாம் இரண்டு மற்றொன்றும்), so the link is real. But 194 is itself a 'when will it be' wish, not an answer, and it is uncertain that its three map onto 229's three. 'Question and answer' overstates it.

Kural 1 uses அகரம் only as a simile for being first; it does not say the Lord is born of letters or held in them. 595's எழுத்திற்பிறவாண்டி therefore neither limits nor answers it, and the link is the shared word எழுத்து.
links.text_issue: 595 line 2 நாட்டினரிகள் likely a misprint for நாட்டின் நரிகள் (jackals).

links.reason: Both trace the embryo stage by stage, from the drop (விந்து … பனியிலொர்பாதி சிறுதுளி / துளிபயறு) to limbs, ten months (மாதம் ஒன்பதும் ஒன்றும் / பதினவனி), birth and the toddler. It is a genuine shared genre of the life-course told to show its end, and the note is accurate.
links.text_issue: 808 has two lacunae marked [***].

links.reason: கல்லிலுஞ் செம்பிலுமோ இருப்பான் and செங்கலும் கருங்கலும் … செம்பிலும் தராவிலும் சிவன்இருப்பன் என்கிறீர் make the same denial in nearly the same words. The pairing teaches more than the stock attack: Pattinathar gives the positive places (சொல், வேதச் சுருதி, அன்பர்), and Sivavakkiyar gives self-knowledge.
links.text_issue: 334 அல்லிலும் may be corrupt.

links.reason: 812 closes asking சிறைக் கருப்பாசயஞ் சேரா மறித்தும் புகாஅ வாழ்வு, and 833 describes the கருப்பாசயமெனு மிருட்சிறை cell by cell and ends இச்சிறை பிழைப்பித் தினிச்சிறை புகாமல். Within one work, this is a genuine development.

745 says the Lord himself set out the outer sects and declared an inner one (கட்சமயம் / உட்சமயம்). 1537 says the hundred sects fall within six and the supreme end is not theirs. One makes the sects the Lord's work, the other denies them the end, and the note admits this, so the agreement is thin. 1537's last line is also unclear.

Near-verbatim across poets: எள்ளுக்குளெண்ணைய்போல் எங்குநிறைந்திருந்த and எள்ளகத்தில் எண்ணெய்போல் எங்குமாகி, both followed by the failure to know it within (உள்ளமறியாது / உள்ளகத்திலேயிருக்க). The figure is stock, but the shared phrasing and shared use make it a meaningful same_image.

Both name the three nadis (இடை, பிங்கலை, சுழுமுனை / நடுநாடி), but they make different claims. 718 identifies the Lord with them and confesses ignorance, while 857 describes the practice of raising மூலம் to the head. The note's 'both hold the three channels as the frame of the practice' adds practice to 718.

கோத்த நிலை in both is a real verbal link. But the qualification depends on the marker's reading of கோத்தார்க்குக் கோத்தநிலை as 'he takes whatever doctrine frames him', and 547's கோத்த நிலைகுலைந்த கொள்கை யறியேண்டி is itself ambiguous. The note's conclusion that the collapse is hers rather than the doctrine-holders' fault is an interpretation laid on top.

The puppet is in both, but 213's காற்றில் உழல் சூத்திரம் is a body whirled by wind or breath, while 2344's பொய்க்கரி யாட்டும் வினை (uncertain: a puppet elephant) is a simile for the Lord's moving the elements. The puppet is a common figure and the uses diverge.
509's line தத்துவங்க ளெல்லாந் தலைகெட்டு வெந்ததடி reappears verbatim in Azhuganni 36 alongside வாகாதி ஐவரையும் மாண்டுவிழக் கண்டேண்டி. It is a real textual doublet, and the note describes it plainly.

316's three Nayanar feats of bodily sacrifice (வாளால் மகவரிந்து, கண்ணிடத்து அப்ப) set against 'how shall I become a servant' are met by 272: even என்பே விறகா இறைச்சி அறுத்திட்டு does not reach him without அன்போடு உருகி. A pointed and instructive pairing.

The same refrain-question in one work, ஈயாமனிதரை யேன் படைத்தாய் and இடும்பரை என்வகுத்தாய், widens from the ungiving to the cruel and lustful, both with barren-tree similes (காயாமரம் / நெடும்பனை). The note is accurate.
links.text_issue: 257 line 2 கம்பன்னராய்க் obscure, possibly corrupt.

links.reason: The two allegories match point by point: deceit cleared first (வஞ்சக் கட்டை / காமம்வெகுளி … பொய்யெனும் குப்பை), love (அன்பென் பாத்தி / அன்புகொடு மெழுகி), and the verbatim முன்புற மெய்யெனும் (எரு / விதானம்). The five senses are cattle in one and buffaloes in the other (பட்டி யஞ்சு / ஐவகைக் கடா). Only 'grace as sprout' is loose, since 821's sprout is ஞானம்.

Both describe the body's death (ஒன்பது வாசலும் ஒக்க அடைத்தன / பூதமுநாலுசுவாசமும்நின்று), which is generic nilaiyamai. The kin's weeping withdrawal (அன்புடையார்கள் அழுதகன்றார்கள்) is not in 810, where women and boys mock instead, and the note borrows it from the next stanza.
செத்தாரைப்போலே திரி and செத்துத் திரிவர் சிவஞானியோர் are the same formula for the jnani's life in the world, given as instruction in one and as description in the other. The note is accurate.
links.text_issue: 418 கடம்பு may be corrupt.

links.reason: Both judge the ungiving by what is wasted: ஈயாமனிதர் like காயாமரம், a dry tank and a cow without milk, and the wealth of one who gives nothing (அற்றார்க்கொன்று ஆற்றாதான் செல்வம்) like a beauty growing old alone. It is a real cross-book agreement through simile.
links.text_issue: 257 line 2 கம்பன்னராய்க் obscure.

links.reason: A textual doublet: ஐங்கரனை … தங்காமல் வந்தொருவன் தன்சொரூபங் காட்டி against Azhuganni's ஐங்கரனைத் தொண்டனிட்டேன் … தாங்காமல் வந்தொருவன் தற்சொரூபங் காட்டி. The note correctly records the தன்/தற் variant.

Both blame the one who does not think of him (நினையாதவர்க்கு இல்லை நின் இன்பம் / நின்னினைந் … திரியாப் பாவிகள்). The images match: the kite on the palmyra by the fruit, on its traditional reading, and the man starving before the dish and thirsting by water. The pairing is specific.

Both make standing depend on money: பத்தெட்டுடைமை பலருள்ளும் பாடெய்தும் … ஒன்றில்லாதார் செத்த பிணத்தின் கடை, and the kin who turn பகை when அருஞ்செல்வம் நீங்கில். One slip: the Naladiyar reports the world's judgment rather than 'counsels'. The contrast with the free feet (சுதந்திரம்) is apt.

The link rests on நீ, but in 116 நீ யென்று கண்டு addresses the sky-reality as 'you', the Lord in the second person. In the great saying of 2577 (நீ அது ஆனாய்), நீ is the seeker. Treating 116 as 'the first stage' of தத்துவமசி conflates the two pronouns.
links.text_issue: 116 சீ யென்று எழுந்து is uncertain.

links.reason: Both reduce the beloved to the body's contents: Naladiyar's குடரும் கொழுவும் குருதியும் … எத்திறத்தாள் ஈர்ங்கோதையாள், and 250's முலையும் இறைச்சியும் … மலமும் உதிரமும். Pattinathar adds வினை as the woman's substance and his own fall. A real shared asubha figure, accurately noted.

That the Lord ends birth is assumed in almost any devotional verse. 1616 specifically says he cuts off the births of துறந்தவர், which would rather qualify 466's complaint (பிறப்பைத் தவிர்த்தையிலை) than agree with it. The link is generic.

There is a real shared image of the jnani as like the dead: பிணம்போற் கிடந்து, பேய்போற் றிரிந்து against செத்துத் திரிவர். But the note claims both set the jnani against other ascetics or ritualists, and 363 has no such contrast. It is a list of the jnani's own ways, so that half of the note is false.

Both Pattinathar verses show the dying body: 375 has kin disowning (நீயாரு நானார்) and disease settling in, 810 has the mockery (தோகையர் பாலர் கோரணி), the filth (மலசலம்) and the stumbling speech (உரை தடுமாறி). The connection is real, but 810 has no disowning by mother and wife, so it extends 375 rather than making the same claim.
links.text_issue: 810 has misprints: 'பாலர்ககோரணி', 'கைகொன் மொழிந்து', 'றங்கிவிழுந்து' (line split across the slash).

links.reason: விண்டவர்கள் கண்டவரோ? கண்டவர்கள் விண்டவரோ? and கண்டவர்கள் ஒருக்காலும் விண்டிடார் / விண்டவர்கள் ஒருக்காலும் கண்டிடார் are the same maxim, one as a question, one as a statement. The note is accurate, and the pairing shows the maxim moving between poets. Both also have a கொண்ட line beside it.

230 says the Lord stood for each in the way each saw and thought of him (அவர் அவர்க்கு அப்படி நின்றாய்), which is about form. 2005's உன்னும் அளவில் உணரும் is about how far he is known, a measure of degree. The note's 'make the form of the Lord depend on the conceiver' is true of 230 only, so the link rests on a loose likeness.

பேச்சிறந்த பேரொளி and சொல்முடிவாகுமே share only the commonplace that the Supreme is beyond words. 2496's point is the three-void scheme, which 598 does not touch. பேசாப் பிரமம் may mean 'the Brahman not to be spoken of' rather than 'that does not speak'.

There is a medical figure in both, மருந்து in 295 and பவரோக வயித்திய நாத in 277. But Vaidyanatha, physician of the disease of birth, is a stock temple epithet, not 'the Siddhars' medical language'. 295's medicine is against dying (இறவாதிருக்க), while 277 cuts the root of birth. The image is generic and the note's framing overstates it.

655 has a holed bellows (ஒட்டைத் துருத்தி) and opening the house (வீட்டைத் திறந்து); 820 has a bag (பை) with one door closed (படிக்கதவு ஒன்றிடின்). The note itself admits the two prescribe opposite acts. The 'agreement' rests on a yogic gloss of வீடு/வெளி/ஒளி that the Tamil of 655 does not fix, plus a loose bag-and-light likeness.
links.text_issue: Both verses' senses are flagged uncertain; 655's third line is cipher.

links.reason: 2391 plainly denies caste (சாதிகுலம் எங்கட்கில்லை, சுக்குலம்), arguing from one origin. 709's குலமொன்றாய் நீ படைத்த குறை is ambiguous, as the marker says, and மலபாண்டம் is the body as filth, not an argument about caste. The link rests on one reading of 709 and is a stock anti-caste pairing.

The ganja-and-opium pairing is real (கஞ்சா அபினி in both), and 36 sets பஞ்சாமிர்தம் against it. But the note's 'the same three drugs ... in both' is false: 1478 names only ganja and opium, and there is no toddy (கள்). 1478 also mocks fraud kaya-kalpa claimants, which 36 does not.

Both allude to the column-of-fire myth: மால் காணா with the boar digging (பன்றி வடிவெடுத்து பார் இடந்து) in 31, and அடிமுடி காண்பார் அயன்மால் in 88. But 88's point is Vishnu's honesty and Brahma's lie, and 31's is the light he longs to tell of. 'The gods' failure as the measure of the light' is not in 88, so this is a shared myth, not a shared claim.

கடங்கடங்கடோறும் கதிரவன் is verbatim in both, and the verb அடங்கு recurs: 2002 அடங்கிட மூடில் அவற்றில் அடங்கான், 796 அடங்குமிடம். The note correctly separates the two uses: the Lord's freedom from the body, and the heart knowing the source. This is a real borrowing.

Each first grants the Brahmin his full ritual standing, 884 with மறையொடு அங்கம் and எரிவளர்த்தாலும், 1861 with ஆறிடும் வேள்வி அருமறை நூலவர். Each then subordinates it to devotion: in 884 he stands among the வேட்டுவர், in 1861 an ஓர்பிடி given to the நீறிடும் தொண்டர் counts for more. The note is accurate, and the shared structure is specific.
links.text_issue: 1861's third line is compressed.

links.reason: செல்வரைப் பின்சென்று ... பல்லினைக் காட்டி matches செல்வம் கருதி ... புல்லறிவாளரைப் போற்றிப் புலராமல், and each turns from courting the rich to the Lord (இறைவனை ஏத்துமின் / கயிலாயத்தனே). The note is accurate about both.

1044 asks whether மக்கள் பெண்டீர் சுற்றம் can come along when மறலி calls. 238 answers with the scene: the wife and children who embrace wail, but once at the மயானம் will not step beyond. The question-and-answer framing is fair, though the theme is common.

957's souls rise in him like waves in the sea and are 'mingled and apart' (விரவியும் வேறாய்). 2481's Lord as the many souls is ஒன்றாய் அன்றாம். Both state the one-and-not-one relation without resolving it, as the note says.

Both address Ganesha, as ஐஞ்சு கரத்தான் and கரியதோர் முகத்தையொத்த கற்பகம். But this is the stock invocation convention, and the purposes differ: firmness in 236, the rise of learning and an apology in 965. 'The Siddhar's plainest devotion goes to Ganesha' overstates a formula.

Both blame women's eyes for delusion (கண்ணால் வெருட்டி, மைஅடர்ந்த கண்ணினார் மயக்கிடும்), which is a stock theme. 1026's 'lost themselves' depends on one reading of ஐயிறந்து, and 1026 turns to a positive promise of saving knowledge that 259 lacks.

The two couplets are near-identical: மஞ்சனம் ... மலர்பறித்து ... நெஞ்சு வெறும்பாழ் ... நின்றநிலை காணேண்டி, with 1525 adding the ஆத்தாடி refrain and தூவாமல் for சாத்தாமல். The note describes the doublet accurately, and the shared couplet under two poets' names is worth recording.

Each lists the body's tissues: நரம்பு தசை தோல் எலும்பு in 714, and குடரும் கொழுவும் குருதியும் என்பும் ... நரம்பொடு தோலும் in 46. Each uses the list against delusion. The note rightly notes the turn from another's body (ஈர்ங்கோதையாள்) to one's own (மயங்கினேன்).

அத்தனைபேர் உண்டாலும் most naturally means 'even if all of them eat', which makes him the inexhaustible food or nectar, not 'though all exist'. 2010's தணிவற நின்றான் is about pervasion as all that moves and does not. Both say he is undiminished, but on different grounds, and the note's gloss of 561 is doubtful.
links.text_issue: உண்டாலும் is glossed as 'exist'; 'eat' is likelier.

links.reason: Both place true silence in the mind: முத்தர் மனமிருக்கும் மோனத்தே, and in 1896 வாக்கு மவுனத்து வந்தாலும் மூங்கையாம். But 1896 requires speech and mind to be silent together (வாக்கு மனமும் இரண்டும் மவுனமாம்), so the note's 'not in the mouth' misstates it. 429 extends the point to the limbs rather than agreeing.

ஆறு ஆதாரம் கடந்த ஆனந்தப் பேரொளி matches ஆதாரம் ஆறாறு அதனின்மேல் போகின்ற பொற்பு: in both the splendour is placed above the six supports. The note is accurate, though ஆறாறு may be the thirty-six tattvas.

நேற்றிருந்தாள் இன்று வெந்து நீறானாள் applies the Kural's நெருநல் உளன் ஒருவன் இன்றில்லை to the poet's own mother. The closing எல்லாம் சிவமயமே turns the observation into a Saiva conclusion. The verbal echo is close and the development is real.

வாக்கிறந்து நின்ற மவுனம் and சாற்றரிதாகிய தத்துவம் share only 'beyond speech'. 498 does not mention the five senses subsiding, which is 1442's claim, and the note supplies that through another verse (444). The pairing rests on a generic ineffability.
links.text_issue: 498 prints 'வாக்கிற்து' for வாக்கிறந்து.

links.reason: The note's 'both set kin below deeds' equivocates. In 212 kin are worse than வினை (வினையினும் தீய), karma being the bad thing. In 340 kin go only to the மயானம் while one's தவம் goes further, which is the good companion. The shared ground is only that kin do not help at death, and the 'deeds' parallel is built on the ambiguity.

Both make wearing the ash itself a means to release: in 28, வெண்ணீறு பூசி to gain the விடு not reached in எண்ணூறு யுகம்; in 1666, திருநீற்றை மங்காமல் பூசி, so deeds go and சிவகதி comes. The note is accurate, and the pairing matters because it sets this plain ritual claim beside a Siddhar work.
links.text_issue: 1666 has 'பூசுng', a typing corruption of பூசும்.

links.reason: 347's detached ones bathe, eat and sleep like worldly people and have no நிஷ்டை. 325's claim that the bliss persists 'standing, sitting, lying' rests on the obscure last line (நித்தல் இருத்தல் கிடத்தல் கீழ்க் காலே), which may be a breath term. The parallel depends on that uncertain reading.
links.text_issue: 325's last line is obscure.

links.reason: ஆமை ... ஐந்தடக்கம் echoes the Kural's ஆமைபோல் ஐந்தடக்கல். The note correctly marks what 20 adds: ஆள்கண்டு, the danger seen, and ஊமை உரு, silence, in place of the seven births.

Both treat the household against death, but on different points. 25 mocks the man who sees the corpse carried yet marries and says உண்டு. 380 reclassifies wife, sons and house as பொய், பழங்கதை, கனவு. The shared ground is the general vanity of household life.
தூங்காமல் தூங்கிச் சுகம் and தூங்கிக் கண்டார் ... தம்முள்ளே both name a waking sleep as the yogic state of bliss. The verbal link is close, and the note is accurate.

Both make Siva's bliss an intoxicant that does not fail: உவட்டாத ஆனந்தக் கள் in 804, ஓவாத தேறல் and சுத்த மது in 325. The pairing is pointed because 325 sits in the chapter against drinking (கள்ளுண்ணாமை) and still uses the drink figure.

'A void mistaken for the goal' holds only if ஆதர் in 2498 means the foolish, and if 553's awkward ஒத்தவிட நித்திரை means 'took it for a fitting sleep'. The marker calls the latter a guess, and both verses are flagged uncertain. The idea is attractive, but two uncertain readings carry it.
links.text_issue: 553's second line is grammatically awkward.

links.reason: ஆங்காரம் ... அடியோடு அறுத்தான் and யான் எனது என்னும் செருக்கு அறுப்பான் share the cutting of ego. But in 524 the Lord or guru does the cutting, while in 346 the aspirant does it and gains a world above the gods. 524's ruin of Om and of 'all that is' points to a void, not a heaven. It is a generic theme with differences the note passes over.

நஞ்சினை அமிர்தா நயந்தோய் and ஆரமுதாக நஞ்சு ஆரும் ... ஈசன் கருத்தது are the same figure, in both made a matter of the Lord's will (நயந்து, கருத்து). The note is fair, though the epithet is a common one.
links.text_issue: 2688's line 3 can be construed several ways.

links.reason: 468 begs for the வேடம் (with the அக்கமணி) as the means of seeing the world as something to leave (விடுமுலகம் நோக்கி). 1188 mocks those who put on வெந்தநீறு and வேடம், asking in which mantra the Lord moves. The note states the reading the conflict depends on.

313's list, காடோ செடியோ ... புறத்திண்ணையோ, leaves the place where the body falls indifferent, because the life's companion is fixed (உயிர்த்துணை நின்பதமே). 26 makes the corpse's treatment indifferent once the கூத்தன் has left. The two are related rather than identical, and the note states them accurately.

252's householders feed their own துருத்தி with அறுசுவை but will not feed துறந்தோர். 858's miser sends the வெறுமிடியன் ஒரு தவசி asking அமுது from house to house and leaps at him like a ஞாளி. Both take the mendicant's side, and the note is accurate.

682 laments not keeping the eyes open on the nose-tip (மூக்குமுனையை முழித்திருந்து பாராமல்) as the cause of his ruin. 2339 attacks those who stare at the nose-tip calling it the sushumna (சுழுனையென்ற மூக்குநுனி) and moves the seat to the uvula. The disagreement over the practice is plain in the Tamil.

முப்பாழுக்கு அப்பால் முதற்பாழ் takes Tirumular's முப்பாழ் scheme (2496's மாயப்பாழ், வியோமப்பாழ் and the third) as known and puts the Lord beyond it. The shared technical term makes the development real.

365 asks whether good and evil can come otherwise than as பங்கயத்தோன் wrote, and counts தொழுதல் among the useless. 620 says those who toil without flagging see ஊழ் in retreat (உப்பக்கம் காண்பர்). The note names the reading the conflict depends on and its softening.

Both have grace removing impurity: in 476, கெடுக்கும் மலம் ஒறுக்கி and the Lord's கடைக்கண்; in 1595, மாச்சற்ற என்னைச் சிவமாக்கி and the gift of feet (தாள்தந்து). But 476 is a plea for a glance, and 1595 reports a completed union with the three debts taken over, so 'the same sequence' overstates a generic likeness.

Pattinathar's காடே திருந்தென்ன? ... ஓடே யெடுத்தென்ன? with உள்ளன்பி லாதவர் dismisses forest, wind-eating, rags and bowl without inner love, as the Kural's மழித்தலும் நீட்டலும் வேண்டா dismisses shaven and matted heads if one quits உலகம் பழித்தது. The note's contrast of the inner test (conduct vs love) is accurate and makes the pairing across books worthwhile.
links.text_issue: கந்தைகற்றி looks like a misprint for கந்தை சுற்றி, and வீடே யிருப்பனு for வீடே இருப்பினும்.

links.reason: Both are Pattinathar's disgust verses against lust for women's bodies, but 359 argues by smell alone (நாறும் repeated) while 405's distinctive image, the கருவாய் two fingers above the எருவாய் and the lover செத்துக்கிடக்கின்றாய் in Tiruvarur's chariot street, has no counterpart in 359. The shared thing is the stock asubha catalogue, not a shared figure.

The link rests on the shared epithet வாசாமகோசரம் (beyond speech and mind), a stock Sanskrit term for the Lord; that both call him so is true but generic. The surrounding claims differ (Pattinathar's ஆசூசமில்லான், அறிவுக்கறிவு vs Tirumular's kalanta where ஆசார நேய மறையும் end), and the note adds nothing beyond the shared word.

Pattinathar's தீக்கிரையாவதல்லால் ஏதுக்காம் is renunciant rhetoric about the body's worthlessness in general, not a rule on how bodies should be disposed of; Tirumular's ஞானிதன் ஆகம் தீயினில் வெந்திடின் is a funeral rule for the jnani's body. Different subjects and purposes; reading 'no exception for the jnani' into 385 manufactures the conflict.

530's நகையாரோ கண்டவர்கள்? நாட்டுக்குப் பாட்டலவோ? ... பார்த்தாருக் கேச்சலவோ is plausibly the akam gossip motif, so a real shared topic with 1142's அலரெமக்கு ஈந்ததிவ் வூர். But 1142's point, the town's ignorance of her அருமை and the ironic gift (ஈந்தது), has no echo in 530, and the 'jnani' transfer comes from the marker's framing, not the couplet's words.

Both use the woman whose mind is with another while with her husband: Pattiragiriyar's தன்கணவன் தன் சுகத்தில் தன்மனம்வே றானது போல் as the traditional model for keeping the Lord's feet in thought, the Naladiyar's உள்ளம் ஒருவன் உழையதா ஒண்ணுதலார் as the deceit fools fail to see. The note accurately describes the opposite moral and devotional uses of one figure.

304 closes ஏதுமொன்றறியேன் யாதுநின்செயலே and 350 opens என்செயலாவது யாதொன்றுமில்லை ... உன்செயலே, the same surrender formula in the same poet. The note is accurate that 304 sets it in a plea for union beyond the tattvas while 350 turns it to முன்செய்த தீவினை, which makes the pairing instructive.
